name: Lesotho
summary: The only country entirely above a thousand metres, with Africa's highest single-drop waterfall at Maletsunyane, southern Africa's only ski resort, and dinosaur footprints in the sandstone.
when: Spring and autumn for walking and riding; June to August for snow.

entries.caption: The Kingdom in the Sky
entries.description: Nowhere in Lesotho is below 1,400 metres, which is true of no other country.
entries.subject: the high Maloti mountains with a shepherd's hut on a ridge

entries.caption: The Maloti
entries.description: Basalt highlands cut by river gorges, and the roof of southern Africa.
entries.subject: the Maloti mountains with deep valleys and no trees

entries.caption: Bearded Vulture and Eland
entries.description: The lammergeier breeds on the Drakensberg escarpment, and eland are back in the reserves.
entries.subject: a bearded vulture in flight along a mountain escarpment

entries.caption: Not the Business Here
entries.description: This is a mountain country, not a savanna one. What you go for is the ground and the horses.
entries.subject: eland grazing in high grassland at Sehlabathebe

entries.caption: Thabana Ntlenyana
entries.description: 3,482 metres, the highest point in Africa south of Kilimanjaro.
entries.subject: the summit plateau of Thabana Ntlenyana under snow

entries.caption: Maletsunyane
entries.description: 192 metres in a single drop, and a commercial abseil down beside it.
entries.subject: the single 192-metre drop of the Maletsunyane falls

entries.caption: The Senqu
entries.description: The Orange river rises here and runs the whole width of South Africa afterwards.
entries.subject: the young Senqu river running through a high mountain valley

entries.caption: High Reservoirs
entries.description: Landlocked and mountainous: the water here is Katse and Mohale, and it is sold to South Africa.
entries.subject: the Katse dam wall and reservoir between mountains

entries.caption: Almost None
entries.description: Above the treeline for most of the country, and the small patches left are protected.
entries.subject: a patch of indigenous forest in a sheltered Lesotho gorge

entries.caption: Pony Trekking
entries.description: The Basotho pony is the way to cross this country, and has been for a hundred and fifty years.
entries.subject: riders on Basotho ponies crossing a high mountain pass

entries.caption: The Blanket and the Hat
entries.description: The Basotho blanket is worn seriously and read closely, and the mokorotlo is on the flag.
entries.subject: a man in a patterned Basotho blanket on a mountain road

entries.caption: The Basotho
entries.description: One people, one language, and a kingdom that kept its independence by going uphill.
entries.subject: Basotho herders in blankets with sheep on a high pasture

entries.caption: Papa, Moroho and Motoho
entries.description: Maize papa with wild greens, and motoho — fermented sorghum drink.
entries.subject: a bowl of papa with moroho greens

entries.caption: Morija Arts and Cultural Festival
entries.description: Music, poetry and horse racing at Morija every year, and the country turns up.
entries.subject: horse racing at the Morija cultural festival

entries.caption: Blankets, Hats and Tapestry
entries.description: Woven mohair tapestry, the conical mokorotlo hat, and the blankets themselves.
entries.subject: a woven mohair tapestry on a loom in Lesotho

entries.caption: Thaba Bosiu
entries.description: The flat-topped mountain Moshoeshoe I defended, and where the nation was made.
entries.subject: the flat-topped plateau of Thaba Bosiu above the plain

entries.caption: Maloti-Drakensberg
entries.description: A World Heritage site shared with South Africa, for its landscape and its San rock art.
entries.subject: San rock paintings on a sandstone overhang in Lesotho

entries.caption: Maseru
entries.description: A small capital on the Caledon, with the border post at the end of the main street.
entries.subject: the main street and sandstone buildings of Maseru

entries.caption: Sandstone and Rondavel
entries.description: Colonial sandstone in Maseru, and painted rondavels with stone walls in the mountains.
entries.subject: a stone rondavel with a thatched roof in the Maloti

entries.caption: Sunday on Horseback
entries.description: The horse is transport, not recreation, and every village has them saddled.
entries.subject: villagers on horseback on a mountain track

entries.caption: Ponies and Snow
entries.description: Short pony treks, dinosaur footprints and, in winter, actual snow.
entries.subject: children on Basotho ponies with a guide

entries.caption: Sani and Sehlabathebe
entries.description: The Sani Pass in four-wheel-drive, and the rock formations and rivers of Sehlabathebe.
entries.subject: the hairpins of the Sani Pass climbing the escarpment

entries.caption: Lodges and Trading Posts
entries.description: Malealea and Semonkong grew out of trading posts, and they are the best of it.
entries.subject: a mountain lodge with stone buildings at Semonkong

entries.caption: Water as the Economy
entries.description: The Highlands Water Project sells water to South Africa, and the dams are the landscape now.
entries.subject: the Katse reservoir winding between steep mountainsides

entries.caption: High and Clear
entries.description: The Maloti in autumn, when the grass turns and the air will not hold any haze.
entries.subject: clear autumn light on golden grassland and basalt ridges

entries.caption: Dinosaur Footprints
entries.description: Trackways in the sandstone at Moyeni and Morija, in the open and unfenced.
entries.subject: fossil dinosaur footprints in exposed sandstone rock

entries.caption: Why Lesotho
entries.description: A whole country above a thousand metres, crossed on a pony, with snow in July.
entries.subject: a rider on a Basotho pony against a wide mountain horizon
